title: Name goal, hard constraints, and open choices apart in the worker brief
action: D1 (store 50349b36): a cell's must_haves may carry open_choices. (a) planning-reference.md, where it lists the must_haves keys (around line 299) and in the example cell JSON (around line 347): add `open_choices` — the plan's current design choices the user did not ask for, which a worker may question with evidence; it is optional and the goal-check does not read it as a truth. (b) packages/bee/prompts/worker-cell.md is the prompt bee dispatch prepare actually renders for every cell worker: right after the inlined Cell block, add a short block that names the three parts apart — Goal (must_haves.truths), Hard constraints (must_haves.prohibitions plus locked D-IDs), Open choices (must_haves.open_choices, when present) — and says an open choice may be questioned with evidence through `bee cells dissent`. Mirror the same three-part naming in the Worker Prompt Template Inputs block of swarming-reference.md (around line 590). If a test in verbs/drivers/tests.rs pins the rendered prompt bytes, update that expectation to the new text and nothing else. (c) bee-swarming SKILL.md Execute step 3: one sentence that an open choice may be questioned through `bee cells dissent` with evidence, while a hard-constraint conflict stays a locked-decision `[BLOCKED]`. D2 (store b79877b1): write no text that orders a worker to look for faults, doubt the lead, or dissent; phrase it as a right used on evidence. Keep every edit short and in the files' existing voice. Run `bee dev regen` so the plugin skill copies, vendored prompts, and release manifest match, and commit the regenerated outputs in the same commit. No code comments. One commit with the trailer `cell: sag-2`. A parallel worker (cell sag-1) edits verbs/report_outcomes.rs, verbs/mod.rs, router.rs and generated/registry_payload.json in the same worktree at the same time: never stage, commit, or revert those paths, even when regen touches them; stage only your own files by name.
